# CANVAS-C01 persistence contract (app schema 3 / IndexedDB structure 1)

Use `createCanvasPersistence()`, `await initialize()`, then `readGlobal`, `readWorkspace`, `readDocuments`, `commit`, and `subscribeInvalidations`. Errors are always `Result<T>`; **never** infer a commit from the absence of an exception. `commit` resolves only on `IDBTransaction.complete`, not `IDBRequest.success`.

- Every `Mutation` has `expectedRevision`. `null` means **create only**; records are born at revision 0; updates/deletions demand an exact revision and increment it. A deleted UUID is tombstoned and cannot be reused. Workspace deletion requires explicit `deleteDocument` mutations with exact expected revisions for **every** live child in the same atomic commit; otherwise the entire transaction fails. There are no implicit unversioned cascades. Workspace and document IDs must be UUIDs created via the exported constructors. Panels/windows also use UUIDs. Window focus is deliberately not persisted.
- `data` is deliberately a **plain JSON object**, not an invented WorkspaceService, PanelService, or DocumentStore schema. All records have `{id, schemaVersion: 3, revision, updatedAt, data}`; documents additionally have `workspaceId`. `data` cannot contain Date, Map, undefined, cycles, NaN or unsafe prototypes. Future service agents must establish and validate their own domain schema _inside_ the `data` envelope. Do not use `id` as Dockview's view/sequence string.
- A commit may create a workspace and its documents in the same request; use `createWorkspace` and `createDocument` (order-independent). A document's `workspaceId` cannot change. Conflicting changes to the same ID fail in the IndexedDB transaction with `CONFLICT`. Independent document writes may proceed. All mutations in a request are all-or-nothing; duplicate targets are rejected.
- Invalidation listeners receive changed store/id pairs only. Every window has a UUID. BroadcastChannel is optional and may lose messages. On foreground/resume/visibility or after suspected missed messages, explicitly reread IndexedDB; never maintain correctness through BroadcastChannel.
- Legacy migrations **are not automatic**. `readLegacyValues([keys])` reads exact localStorage strings without parsing or deleting them. `beginLegacyMigration(key)` atomically captures an immutable `backups` record and a `started` `migration` record, or reports an interruption/duplicate. `readBackup` and `readMigration` inspect them. `resumeLegacyMigration(key, revision)` explicitly reclaims an interrupted attempt via revision CAS. A conversion agent must populate domain records and pass `migration: { key, expectedRevision: lease.revision }` in the **same `commit`**; the marker becomes `imported` only if the imported data commits. Unknown/bad legacy JSON must remain as its original `raw` string; the converter decides whether to import, quarantine or request intervention. Never delete legacy keys in C01.

## Replacing the current writers (CAN-02/03/04)

Current partial cutover: `DockCanvas.tsx` now uses `live-layouts.ts` as its **sole active layout writer**. The old `canvas-dockview-layout-v2-<profile-id>` (or global v1) keys are read **only** as immutable legacy inputs, backed up with a migration lease and committed into a deterministic UUID-keyed `workspaces` layout record. No component may write or delete those old layout keys. `profiles.ts` Zustand `canvas-profiles-v1` (profiles, routes, notes, drafts) and `config.ts` `canvas-config` preferences are still their **own localStorage writers** and have NOT been promoted; do not falsely claim the whole app uses C01. Complete the remaining domains without adding competing writers: (1) freeze each domain's existing localStorage writer before its migration, (2) snapshot and back up raw data, (3) validate/migrate with explicit UUID mapping and proper document ownership, (4) commit conversion and imported markers atomically, (5) activate one IDB writer for that domain, and (6) retain the old localStorage bytes for rollback/quarantine. Do not leave both storage paths writable, and do not automatically reinterpret old profile IDs (e.g. `global`, `study`) as UUIDs.

The integration boundary is opaque validated `data`: CAN-02 owns workspace structure and lifecycle, CAN-03 owns panel identity/layout, CAN-04 owns document ownership and draft/save semantics. These agents must agree on shapes before writing data. A global record is created once at revision 0. A new adapter instance must call `initialize()`. After `close()`, instantiate another adapter rather than reusing the closed one. Persisted records are shared between windows; view focus remains per-window.

`CanvasPersistence` accepts injected `databaseName`, `indexedDB`, `windowId`, and `broadcastChannelFactory` for isolated tests. Use the default name in production. The `localStorage` migration primitive reads the ambient browser storage, never an injected fake for transaction correctness.

## Active CAN-03 Dockview layout behavior

`live-layouts.ts` has a deterministic cryptographic UUID namespace for layout workspaces; it does not cast old `global`/`study` profile IDs to UUIDs. It initializes the C01 adapter, reads the existing canonical record, or backs up one exact v2/v1 legacy key through `beginLegacyMigration` and commits a `createWorkspace` with the migration lease in the **same transaction**. Invalid or interrupted legacy imports block hydration with a visible recovery warning and never delete source bytes. Subsequent layout changes use versioned `updateWorkspace` CAS; conflicting cross-tab saves must fail visibly. The live UI does not report a successful reset until the transaction completes. Old profile removal cannot delete the legacy layout raw record. The active source-only Chromium gate is `.github/tests/live-layouts-browser.mjs`.

This is deliberately **not** document-draft cutover, whole-workspace ownership integration with GHCode, profile directory replacement, preferences cutover, or unified shell activation. Keep those gates open until tests prove all single-writer boundaries.
